situation.whoThisIs: An aesthetic or cosmetic clinic operated as a Grom Digital client account. The clinic treats patients; Grom runs the acquisition system on its behalf.
situation.howLeadsArrive: Meta lead-form ads and clinic landing pages, feeding an AI-handled conversation that books consultations.
situation.whatIsSold: Aesthetic treatments and consultations, typically with a deposit taken to hold the appointment.
situation.theFunnel: enquiry -> conversation -> booked consultation -> attended -> treatment decision -> paid treatment
situation.objective: Booked consultations that attend and convert into paid treatment, judged on revenue per enquiry.
knownDataCaveats: Opportunity `monetaryValue` is the revenue basis, never the payments surface. Where it is unset revenue is UNMEASURABLE rather than zero.
This system is DESIGNED to handle leads with automation and AI. Inserting a human is not a generic fix and must be argued from the evidence.

targets.basis: Every enquiry is contacted by automation, so a shortfall is a delivery or enrolment failure, not a demand problem. Speed is the real lever: close rates run 32% when the first reply lands inside five minutes against 12% at 24 hours.

Aesthetic clinics run 15 to 25 percent no-shows, worse than general medical practice because treatment is elective, so showing 75 to 85 percent is the normal band and 85 is the top of it. A held deposit is the main thing that moves it. No-shows cost aesthetic clinics 15 to 20 percent of annual revenue, which makes this the single most defensible number on the ladder.
The inverse of the show target, stated separately because it is its own declared edge. Under 10 percent is what a well-run clinic with deposits and a working reminder ladder reaches.

Average clinics convert 40 to 55 percent of attended consultations into booked treatment; 50 is the top of average. Top performers reach 75 to 85 percent, and the published gap is attributed to the consultation process itself rather than to marketing.
